Inbox: a text size setting

The Inbox draws its text at one size today, and nobody can change it. This plan adds a Text size row to Settings with 12, 13, 14 and 15, where 14 stays the default. A pick changes the whole window at once and is saved for the next time.

  1. DecidedOne setting sizes the whole Inbox: 12, 13, 14 or 15, and 14 is the default.01
  2. ChangeSettings gets a Text size row. A pick shows at once, with no reload.04
  3. ChangeThe server saves the size in config.json and refuses any other value.05
  4. KeptAt 14 the window draws exactly as it does today.06
  5. OpenIs 14 the right default? Try each size, then decide.07

read · 01 / 07

Why a text size setting

01 / 07

  1. Settings, General, Appearance holds one row today: Theme. Nothing there changes how large the text is.

    Someone who finds the Inbox too small or too large has no way to change it. The text size is fixed in the stylesheet.

  2. A second row, Text size, with a button for each size: 12, 13, 14 and 15. It looks like the Theme control above it.

    The size applies to the whole Inbox, at once, with no reload. Use the buttons on the right to compare.

read · 02 / 07

How the Inbox sizes its text today

02 / 07

  1. Every text size in the stylesheet already comes from one number, --ib-type. Today it is 14.

    A hidden switch can take it down to 13, so the owner could compare. No person can reach that switch from the window.

  2. The list rows, subjects, the sidebar, message bodies, question cards, Settings, and the small labels all scale from it. Their steps stay the same relative to each other.

    Nothing shrinks past its floor: no text goes under 11 px, and phone controls stay at 16 px, so iOS does not zoom.

The setting, from the screen to the page

04 / 07

  1. The row draws its buttons from one shared list of sizes, so the screen and the server agree. A pick calls chooseTextSize.

    Its description changes with the pick: at 14 it says this is the default.

  2. The page puts the size on the document as one style value, --inbox-text-size. The stylesheet reads it, so every size changes in the same frame.

    At 14 the value is removed, not set. The stylesheet then falls back to its own 14, which is why 14 draws exactly as today.

  3. Step through one pick of 15. The screen changes first, then the page and the server both remember it.

    A cookie lets the next visit paint at 15 at once. config.json is the size every browser on this computer starts from.

The server keeps the size

05 / 07

  1. The settings route takes text_size and saves it in config.json as inboxTextSize. Anything but 12, 13, 14 or 15 is refused with 422, and nothing is saved.

    Try a value on the right to see the answer.

  2. One function checks the value, saves it, and reads the file back. If the file did not change, the route says so instead of claiming success.

  3. On the next visit, the cookie paints the page before the first render. Then the first settings read answers with config.json's size, and that wins.

    One exception: a size the person picked on this page before that read answered is never undone by it.

What stays the same

06 / 07

  1. Nobody has to do anything. Until someone picks a size, the window is 14, and at 14 every size is exactly today's.

    Row and control heights do not change at any size, so phones keep their 44 px targets.
